name: Cutaway Explainer 3D
description: Low-poly cutaway explainer: a clean matte toon-like look in soft daylight with one warm key and soft shadows, a camera that opens close on a recurring cartoon character and pulls out to reveal the whole cross-section, and a diegetic overlay kit (a top strip of flow-diagram chips with live values, a concept-name pill, a demand bar that turns red over its limit, a not-equal comparison card) plus signal dots running down in-world pipes. A format, not a scene: the agent builds the cutaway set, the character and the pipes from scratch (custom parts) for every video. No emoji.
prompt_hint: 6-8 scenes (4-7 s) about how a system works (power, water, data, money, traffic). EVERY scene: visual.type "scene3d" with the SAME recurring custom character (head, hat, body, arms with wave / walk motion, drawn from scratch with a new design per video) plus the custom parts that explain the step, and a `world` of the cutaway set built from parts (walls with one face removed, floor plates, furniture, pipes as `tube` parts) whose concept names the setting. Use camera "pullout" on the opening scene and shots close / reveal / shoulder / through on others. Fill `overlay`: one `flow` strip (3-5 chips whose active chip moves with the narration), a `concept` pill when a new term is introduced, a `limit` bar for demand versus capacity, a `versus` card for an "X is not Y" idea; add `fx` signal along every pipe. Captions stay at the bottom; when a scene has a `title`, set `title.color` to "accent" or "accent3" (the yellow role is for the overlay). No emoji.
